es.summary: Pequeño dispositivo plástico en forma de T que se coloca dentro del útero para prevenir el embarazo. Es un método anticonceptivo de larga duración y reversible.
key_points: Tipos: T de cobre (sin hormonas, dura hasta 10 años) y DIU con levonorgestrel (hormonal, dura de 3 a 8 años).
Su eficacia supera el 99 %; la fertilidad regresa de inmediato al retirarlo.
Deja dos hilos que salen por el cérvix hacia la vagina: sirven para revisar que siga en su lugar y para retirarlo.
Puede colocarse inmediatamente después del parto o de un aborto.
Si hay infección en vagina, cérvix o útero, se pospone la inserción hasta tratarla.

usage: Se anota en la historia clínica dentro del método de planificación familiar (MPF): «Usuaria de DIU».
Ejemplo: «DIU T de cobre colocado posparto el 06/10/2026».
En los antecedentes gineco-obstétricos (AGO) se pregunta por el uso actual o previo de DIU.
nursing_care: Explicar que puede haber cólicos, dolor de espalda y manchado unos días después de la inserción.
Enseñar a revisar los hilos y a no intentar retirarlo si se sale parcialmente.
El riesgo de enfermedad pélvica inflamatoria aumenta en las primeras 3 semanas tras la colocación.
Indicar consultar si hay fiebre, escalofríos, dolor pélvico, sangrado o flujo anormal.
Si ocurre un embarazo con DIU, hay más riesgo de embarazo ectópico: debe valorarse de inmediato.

en.summary: A small plastic T-shaped device placed inside the uterus to prevent pregnancy (DIU in Spanish). It is a long-acting reversible birth control method.
key_points: Types: copper T (hormone-free, effective for 10 years) and levonorgestrel IUD (hormonal, effective for 3 to 8 years).
Effectiveness is above 99%; fertility returns immediately once the device is removed.
Two strings hang outside the cervix within the vagina: they are used to check that the IUD stays in position and to remove it.
It can be inserted right after giving birth or after a miscarriage.
If there is an infection in the vagina, cervix or uterus, insertion is delayed until the infection is cured.

usage: Charted under the family planning method: "IUD user".
Example: "Copper T IUD placed postpartum on 10/06/2026".
The gynecologic-obstetric history (AGO) asks about current or previous IUD use.
nursing_care: Explain that cramping, low backache and spotting can occur for a few days after insertion.
Teach how to check the strings and not to try to remove an IUD that has come part of the way out.
The risk for pelvic inflammatory disease increases in the first 3 weeks after placement.
Tell the patient to seek care for fever, chills, pelvic pain, bleeding or abnormal discharge.
Pregnancy with an IUD carries a higher risk of ectopic pregnancy and needs prompt evaluation.

summary.0.quote: An intrauterine device (IUD) is a small plastic T-shaped device used for birth control . It is inserted into the uterus (womb) where it stays to prevent pregnancy.

summary.1.quote: Table 5.13 summarizes the pros, cons, and efficacy of the different LARCs.

key_points.2.quote: Removes the tube, leaving two small strings that dangle outside the cervix within the vagina.

key_points.3.quote: For the most part, an IUD can be inserted at any time: Right after giving birth After an elective or spontaneous miscarriage

key_points.4.quote: If you have an infection in your vagina, cervix or uterus, you should not have an IUD inserted until the infection is cured.

sections.nursing_care.0.quote: Some women have mild cramping, low backache, and spotting for a couple of days.

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: DO NOT try to remove an IUD that has come part of the way out or has slipped out of place.

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: The risk for pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) , an infection of the female reproductive organs, when a person has intrauterine contraception is not necessarily increased overall, but it does increase in the first 3 weeks after placement (CDC, 2021).

sections.nursing_care.3.quote: The nurse provides education to the patient before they leave the office about calling to report heavy bleeding; pain with intercourse; abdominal pain; signs of infection including fever, chills, and malaise; and missing strings.

sections.nursing_care.4.quote: A higher risk of an ectopic pregnancy , but only if you do get pregnant while using an IUD.
